sections.overview: Aequidens diadema is a South American freshwater cichlid known from the upper Rio Negro and tributaries of the Orinoco. Its scientific name refers to a diadem, and it is sometimes sold as the royal acara. Older records from Peru require taxonomic caution because some may refer to a different species.
sections.identification: It has the compact, oval, laterally compressed body typical of an acara, with olive to brassy tones, a dark mark on each flank and a darker band across the head that gives the fish its diadem-like name. FishBase records a maximum standard length of 11.8 cm for a male or unsexed fish; that is body length excluding the caudal fin. The sources found no comparable female measurement, body width, height or reliable mass, so they do not support a numerical sex comparison. Similar Aequidens can share dark flank marks; use the head pattern together with locality and a taxonomic key.
sections.habitat: The verified distribution includes the upper Negro River in the Amazon basin and tributaries of the Orinoco in Colombia and Venezuela. It is a tropical freshwater, benthopelagic fish, living close to the bottom as well as in the water column. FishBase gives a broad temperature range of about 23–28 °C; fine-scale habitat descriptions and depth records are sparse.
sections.diet: A species-specific study of wild prey or stomach contents was not found in the sources reviewed. FishBase provides no direct prey list for this species; its displayed trophic-level estimate is modelled from related fishes and should not be treated as a measured diet. A detailed menu therefore cannot be stated reliably from the available evidence.
sections.behavior: The clearest documented parental behavior occurs after spawning: both parents take the newly hatched larvae into their mouths. This is a specialized form of brood care and distinguishes its reproductive behavior from simple egg guarding. Beyond parental care, the reviewed species accounts provide little direct field information on daily activity, social grouping or territorial behavior.
sections.reproduction: The species lays eggs on a substrate rather than brooding the eggs in the mouth. After hatching, both parents carry the larvae in their mouths, a delayed, biparental form of larval mouthbrooding reported in the cichlid literature. The sources reviewed do not provide dependable species-specific clutch size, incubation time or age at maturity.
sections.ecology: The species occupies freshwater river systems in the Amazon–Orinoco region and is classified as benthopelagic. Its exact ecological role and natural diet are not quantified in the sources found. FishBase flags older Peruvian records as potentially belonging to a different taxon, so those records should not be used uncritically to extend its range or ecological profile.
sections.conservation: The IUCN assessment dated 2020 classifies Aequidens diadema as Least Concern. The assessment summary reports a broad range but limited information on population size and trend; the category should not be read as proof that every local population is abundant or monitored. No reliable species-wide trend was found in the sources reviewed.
